# Strategy Analyzer run sheet (manual fallback)

The operator can do these runs itself: `python backtest_runner.py <bundle dir> --import` (see README, Backtests). Use this sheet only to run them by hand.

Generated from the five Lucid handoff bundles (2026-11-06). Each strategy is two legs on one MNQ chart, so each needs two Strategy Analyzer runs (10 total).

## Settings common to every run

- Instrument: **`MNQ 12-26`** (the current front month), 1 minute bars. NinjaTrader merges the earlier contracts into it, so a
  2020-2026 run has data back to 2019. Do not use `MNQ ##-##`: it returned empty results through the add-on.
- Date range: 2020-01-02 to 2026-10-16
- Slippage: **2** ticks (the 11-05 run had 0)
- Commission: **0.62 per side**. The only templates installed are the three NinjaTrader Brokerage ones, all $0 per side. Create a template
  (e.g. "Lucid 0.62", MNQ 0.62 per side) first. The 11-05 run used "NinjaTrader Brokerage Free" = no costs.
- Trading hours: "CME US Index Futures ETH". The PC is on Central time, which these scripts assume (all times are CT).
- Include trade history: **ON** (Strategy Analyzer properties). With it off the Trades grid is empty and there is nothing to export.
- Backtest type: Backtest, order fill resolution Standard, start behavior WaitUntilFlat
- Sanity check before the long run: do one 3-month run on `MNQ 12-26` first. The ORB legs trade Tue-Fri only (about 0.6 trades per day
  across both legs), so you should see roughly 30 trades in 3 months. If you see 0, the problem is data or settings, not the strategy. (Checked 2026-06-03..2026-10-22, S742 ORB leg: 26 trades, net -151 before commission.)

## After each run

Export the Trades grid (right click the results, Export) to `backtests/<leg>__trades.csv` in the matching bundle, then call `import_backtest` for that spec version.
